questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which nerve prevents Trendelenburg sign by innervating tensor fasciae latae, gluteus medius, and gluteus minimus?
questions.explanation: The superior gluteal nerve innervates gluteus medius and minimus, keeping the pelvis level during single-leg stance.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Loss of gluteus maximus function results in difficulty performing which of the following activities?
options: Climbing stairs or rising from a seat
questions.explanation: Gluteus maximus extends the hip forcibly, necessary for standing up from a chair or climbing stairs.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Anterior hip dislocation carries the highest risk of damaging which structure?
questions.explanation: Anterior hip dislocations compromise anterior neurovascular structures, including the femoral nerve and vessels.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which artery provides the primary blood supply to the femoral head in adults?
questions.explanation: Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery provide the main blood supply to the femoral head.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with foot drop and loss of sensation over the dorsum of the foot has damage to which nerve?
questions.explanation: Common fibular nerve injury causes foot drop (deep branch) and dorsal cutaneous sensory loss (superficial branch).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle inserts onto the base of the 5th metatarsal and everts the foot?
questions.explanation: Fibularis brevis inserts directly into the tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal bone.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Inability to stand on tiptoes and loss of sensation on the sole of the foot indicates lesion to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The tibial nerve innervates plantarflexors (gastrocnemius, soleus) and supplies sensation to the sole.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which structure passes through the saphenous opening in the fascia lata?
questions.explanation: The great saphenous vein ascends medially and drains into the femoral vein via the saphenous opening.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which ligament prevents anterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur?
questions.explanation: The ACL prevents anterior translation of the tibia on the femur (positive anterior drawer sign).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Posterior drawer test positivity in knee examination indicates damage to which structure?
questions.explanation: The posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) prevents posterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which three structures are classically involved in the 'unhappy triad' knee injury?
questions.explanation: The classic unhappy triad involves tears of the ACL, MCL, and medial meniscus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle unlocks the knee joint from full extension by laterally rotating the femur on a fixed tibia?
questions.explanation: Popliteus unlocks the knee by laterally rotating the femur (or medially rotating the tibia).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The saphenous nerve is a purely sensory branch originating from which main nerve?
questions.explanation: The saphenous nerve is the terminal cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve supplying the medial leg.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A femoral hernia emerges through the femoral ring into the femoral canal, situated medially to what structure?
questions.explanation: From lateral to medial, the femoral sheath contents are Artery, Vein, Empty space (canal), Lymphatics.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following muscles is a powerful flexor of the hip and inserts on the lesser trochanter?
questions.explanation: The iliopsoas (psoas major + iliacus) inserts on the lesser trochanter and is the main hip flexor.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The adductor magnus is a dual-innervated muscle supplied by the obturator nerve and which other nerve?
questions.explanation: Adductor magnus has an adductor part (obturator nerve) and a hamstring part (tibial nerve).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Sensory loss over the medial aspect of the thigh combined with weakness in thigh adduction points to injury of which nerve?
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve innervates the medial compartment (adductors) and medial thigh skin.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The small saphenous vein drains into which deep venous structure posterior to the knee?
questions.explanation: The small saphenous vein ascends posteriorly along the calf and empties into the popliteal vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which ligament is most frequently injured in excessive inversion ankle sprains?
questions.explanation: The ATFL is the weakest lateral ankle ligament and the first to tear during inversion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Eversion ankle injuries risk tearing which strong, multi-part medial ligament group?
questions.explanation: The deltoid ligament protects against ankle eversion injuries.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which nerve lies directly behind the lateral malleolus?
questions.explanation: The sural nerve passes posterior to the lateral malleolus along with the short saphenous vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The calcaneal (Achilles) tendon reflex tests the functional integrity of which spinal cord levels?
questions.explanation: The Achilles tendon reflex predominantly evaluates the S1 and S2 nerve roots.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which structure forms the lateral roof border of the popliteal fossa?
questions.explanation: The biceps femoris muscle forms the superolateral boundary of the popliteal fossa.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Loss of cutaneous sensation in the first webbed space between the 1st and 2nd toes isolates damage to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The deep fibular nerve supplies sensory fibers strictly to the skin web space between digits 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which nerve innervates the fibularis longus and fibularis brevis muscles in the lateral compartment of the leg?
questions.explanation: The superficial fibular nerve motor supply is restricted to muscles of the lateral compartment.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Where can the dorsalis pedis artery pulse be reliably palpated on physical examination?
options: Medial to extensor hallucis longus tendon
Lateral to extensor hallucis longus tendon
questions.explanation: The dorsalis pedis pulse is felt lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon on the dorsum of the foot.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which ligament maintains the medial longitudinal arch of the foot and is known as the 'spring ligament'?
questions.explanation: The plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament supports the head of the talus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Tarsal tunnel syndrome involves entrapment and compression of which nerve beneath the flexor retinaculum?
questions.explanation: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is compression of the tibial nerve behind the medial malleolus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle of the anterior compartment of the leg dorsiflexes and inverts the foot?
questions.explanation: Tibialis anterior dorsiflexes and inverts the foot at the ankle joint.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which hamstring muscle inserts onto the head of the fibula?
questions.explanation: The tendon of biceps femoris attaches to the lateral side of the fibular head.
